name: child with a limp overview
title: A child with a limp or hip pain: first exclude a septic hip with the Kocher criteria, then age separates transient synovitis, Legg-Calve-Perthes disease and slipped capital femoral epiphysis; each column gives presentation, investigations and treatment

nodes.title: A child with a limp: is it a SEPTIC hip? If not, AGE narrows the rest
lines: every one: blood count, ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) and CRP (C-reactive protein), hip x-ray ± ultrasound

nodes.title: FEVER, unwell, will not walk
lines: infection until proven otherwise

nodes.title: Afebrile and well: AGE decides
lines: 3-10: transient synovitis · 4-8: Perthes · 8-15, obese: slipped epiphysis

nodes.title: Septic hip or osteomyelitis
lines: the one not to miss

nodes.title: Transient synovitis
lines: non-infectious hip inflammation after a virus
the most common cause of hip pain under 10

nodes.title: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
lines: IDIOPATHIC avascular necrosis of the femoral head
the most common childhood hip disorder

nodes.title: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis
lines: the head slips posterior and inferior on the neck

nodes.title: Kocher criteria
lines: • temperature > 38.5 °C
• white count > 12 × 10⁹/L · ESR > 40 mm/h
• cannot walk on it
~ C-reactive protein added later

nodes.title: Age 3-10, boys 2:1
lines: • SUDDEN hip pain 7-10 days after a cold or sore throat
• pain to thigh or knee, better through the day
• afebrile or LOW fever (< 38), looks well

nodes.title: Exam
lines: hip held flexed, abducted, externally rotated · less internal rotation, abduction

nodes.title: Age 4-8, boys 5:1
lines: • GRADUAL painless limp, then pain over weeks to months
• mild pain referred to the KNEE, worse with activity, better with rest
• family history, low birth weight, second-hand smoke
• early on can look like transient synovitis

nodes.title: Exam
lines: looks well · less abduction and internal rotation
apparent leg length difference (tight adductors)

nodes.title: Age 8-15 (girls ~12, boys ~14), OBESE
lines: • gradual painful limp: hip, thigh or KNEE pain
• obesity #1 · growth spurt, endocrine disease, radiation, family history
• left more often · 1 in 5 both hips
• atypical age or weight → endocrine cause (hypothyroid, growth hormone deficiency)

nodes.title: Exam
lines: • antalgic, may not bear weight · thigh wasting
• hip rolls into EXTERNAL rotation on flexion (Drehmann sign)
• less internal rotation, abduction

nodes.title: URGENT workup
lines: see the MSK INFECTIONS chart

nodes.title: Bloodwork, x-ray, ultrasound
lines: • NORMAL (ESR, CRP may be slightly up)
• done to rule out septic arthritis

nodes.title: X-ray: anteroposterior (AP) pelvis + frog-leg
lines: flattened, fragmented femoral head · bone scan, MRI

nodes.title: X-ray: AP pelvis + frog-leg
lines: • earliest: WIDE, irregular physis
• Klein's line along the neck MISSES the head (Trethowan sign)
• 'melting ice cream cone' · MRI if unclear

nodes.title: Never call it transient synovitis
lines: until infection is excluded

nodes.title: Anti-inflammatory (NSAID) + reassure
lines: self-limiting in 7-10 days · full recovery

nodes.title: Refer to orthopedics
lines: • keep the range of motion (physiotherapy)
• off-load: crutches, brace, swim, cycle
• NSAIDs, acetaminophen · osteotomy for some
better motion = better outcome

nodes.title: Poorly treated
lines: early osteoarthritis

nodes.title: STOP weight-bearing + EMERGENCY orthopedics
lines: further slip → avascular necrosis (25%)
also arthritis · fixed physis stops growing

nodes.title: Fix it where it lies: do NOT force a reduction
lines: • stable: one screw in situ
• unstable: open reduction + internal fixation

panels.title: The rest of the differential, by age
items: under 4: transient synovitis · infection · juvenile idiopathic arthritis · non-accidental injury · pain referred from the limb
4-10: transient synovitis · Perthes · infection · 10-16: slipped epiphysis · avulsion fracture · infection
uncommon at any age: leukemia · under 4: neuroblastoma metastases, eosinophilic granuloma · 4-16: Ewing sarcoma · teens: osteoid osteoma, osteosarcoma

panels.title: Any abnormal gait: warning signs
items: asymmetry · progression · leg length difference · pain · deformity · a suspected associated condition
also: missed hip dysplasia (painless waddle, leg length difference), clubfoot, overuse, trauma, neuromuscular, inflammatory arthritis (see the PEDIATRIC ORTHOPEDICS chart)
